questions.q: In a SAML-based SSO exchange, what role does ServiceNow play?
options: The Identity Provider (IdP)
The signing certificate authority
The Service Provider (SP)
A third-party auditor of the exchange
questions.explain: ServiceNow is the Service Provider — the application the user wants to reach — while a separate system (e.g. Okta, Entra ID) acts as the Identity Provider.

questions.q: What does a Multi-Provider SSO configuration record store?
options: A list of all ACLs in the instance
Every user's plaintext password
The IdP's entity ID, SSO endpoint URL, and signing certificate
The user's MFA device registrations
questions.explain: This record holds the metadata ServiceNow needs to establish trust with a specific IdP and verify its signed assertions.

questions.q: In the SAML login flow, at which step does the user actually enter their password?
options: When ServiceNow first loads the login page
The password is never entered anywhere in a SAML flow
ServiceNow collects it before redirecting anywhere
At the IdP, after ServiceNow redirects the browser there
questions.explain: The user authenticates at the IdP's SSO endpoint after being redirected there; ServiceNow itself never collects or sees the password.

questions.q: How does ServiceNow confirm that an incoming SAML assertion really came from the trusted IdP?
options: It trusts any assertion without validation, since redirection alone is proof enough
It validates the assertion's signature against the IdP's signing certificate stored in the Multi-Provider SSO configuration record
It re-checks the user's password directly
It calls the IdP's support line to confirm
questions.explain: ServiceNow cryptographically validates the signed assertion using the certificate configured in the Multi-Provider SSO record — that's the real mechanism behind the trust.

questions.q: A SAML login starts failing for everyone. Based on the components covered in this lesson, what's one of the most likely real causes to check first?
options: The user's group membership in sys_user_grmember
The user's role assignments in sys_user_has_role
An expired or mismatched signing certificate, or a misconfigured entity ID/endpoint URL in the Multi-Provider SSO record
A missing field-level ACL on the Incident table
questions.explain: Since SAML trust depends entirely on the Multi-Provider SSO configuration record's certificate and endpoint data, those are the first places a broken trust relationship shows up.
